context.title: The King Comes Home
context.summary: Joab warns David that his grief is shaming his loyal troops, so David goes out to sit in the gate. As David returns, he pardons Shimei, hears Mephibosheth's side of the story, and honors the aged Barzillai. Judah and the northern tribes quarrel over who has more claim on the king.
context.background: In Hebrew Bibles, David's lament in 18:33 begins chapter 19, so verse numbers here differ by one. Mephibosheth had not trimmed his beard or washed his clothes since David fled (v. 24), signs of mourning that supported his claim of loyalty. The quarrel at the end (vv. 41–43) foreshadows the later split of the kingdom.

customs.note: The king took his public place at the city gate, where people could see him and bring their cases.

watchFor: Mercy to Shimei for now (v. 23), revisited at David's death (1 Kings 2:8-9).
'We have ten parts in the king' (v. 43): north against south.

people.name: Joab
people.summary: One of the three sons of Zeruiah, David’s sister, and “captain of the host” during the whole of David’s reign (2 Sam. 2:13; 10:7; 11:1; 1 Kings 11:15).

people.name: Absalom
people.summary: Father of peace; i.e., “peaceful” David’s son by Maacah (2 Sam. 3:3; comp. 1 Kings 1:6). He was noted for his personal beauty and for the extra-ordinary profusion of the hair of his head (2 Sam. 14:25,26).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: A son of Ahitub, of the line of Eleazer (2 Sam. 8:17; 1 Chr. 24:3), high priest in the time of David (2 Sam. 20:25) and Solomon (1 Kings 4:4).

people.name: Abiathar
people.summary: Father of abundance, or my father excels, the son of Ahimelech the high priest. He was the tenth high priest, and the fourth in descent from Eli.

people.name: Amasa
people.summary: The son of Abigail, a sister of king David (1 Chr. 2:17; 2 Sam. 17:25).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: A Benjamite of the house of Saul, who stoned and cursed David when he reached Bahurim in his flight from Jerusalem on the occasion of the rebellion of Absalom (2 Sam. 16:5-13).

people.name: Gera
people.summary: The father of Shimei, who so grossly abused David (2 Sam. 16:5; 19:16, 18).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Ziba
people.summary: Post; statue, “a servant of the house of Saul” (2 Sam. 9:2), who informed David that Mephibosheth, a son of Jonathan, was alive.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.”

people.name: Zeruiah
people.summary: Stricken of the Lord, David’s sister, and the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel (1 Chr. 2:16), who were the three leading heroes of David’s army, and being his nephews, they were admitted to the closest companionship with him.

people.name: Abishai
people.summary: Father of (i.e., “desirous of”) a gift, the eldest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was the brother of Joab and Asahel (2 Sam. 2:18; 1 Chr. 2:16).

people.name: Mephibosheth
people.summary: The son of Jonathan, and grandson of Saul (2 Sam. 4:4). He was but five years old when his father and grandfather fell on Mount Gilboa. The child’s nurse hearing of this calamity, fled with him from Gibeah, the royal residence, and stumbling in her haste, the child was thrown to the ground and maimed in both his feet, and ever after was unable to walk (19:26).

people.name: Barzillai
people.summary: A Gileadite of Rogelim who was distinguished for his loyalty to David. He liberally provided for the king’s followers (2 Sam. 17:27).

places.name: Gilgal
places.summary: From the solemn transaction of the reading of the law in the valley of Shechem between Ebal and Gerizim the Israelites moved forward to Gilgal, and there made a permanent camp (Josh. 9:6; 10:6).

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Bahurim
places.summary: Young men, a place east of Jerusalem (2 Sam. 3:16; 19:16), on the road to the Jordan valley.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Rogelim
places.summary: Fullers, a town of Gilead, the residence of Barzillai the Gileadite (2 Sam. 17:27; 19:31), probably near to Mahanaim.

places.name: Mahanaim
places.summary: Two camps, a place near the Jabbok, beyond Jordan, where Jacob was met by the “angels of God,” and where he divided his retinue into “two hosts” on his return from Padan-aram (Gen. 32:2).

events.title: Reign of David
events.summary: Passage: 2 Samuel 2:1–24:25. People: David. Place: Hebron, Jerusalem. Lasted about 40 years.
